inputs.description: 4 sample posts; one risky post live at /ai-best-in-class

summary.headline: One live post stacks unprovable superlatives, a competitor comparison, and a money-back guarantee — fix before any AI repurposes it.
summary.narrative: The post at /ai-best-in-class trips every claims check at once: superlatives with no proof, a comparative claim against 'every competitor', and an outcome guarantee with a refund promise. An AI drafting from this corpus would replicate that exposure at scale. Stand up a substantiation standard, a banned-claims list, and a Legal review path before enabling any AI content step.

findings.title: Unsubstantiated superlatives stacked in a live post
findings.what_we_found: The post 'The Best-in-Class AI Platform for Revenue Teams' calls the product 'industry-leading, best-in-class' and 'the #1 choice for revenue teams everywhere' with no cited proof.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An AI repurposing or generating from this corpus will replicate unprovable absolute claims at scale, multiplying regulatory and brand exposure across every draft.
the_fix: Remove or qualify each superlative until a dated, sourced proof artifact exists on file.
Add 'best-in-class' (without proof), 'industry-leading', and '#1' to the banned-claims deny-list.
Require a substantiation link on any future superlative before it may appear in a draft.
findings.evidence: "Our industry-leading, best-in-class solution is the #1 choice for revenue teams everywhere."

findings.title: Comparative claim against 'every competitor'
findings.what_we_found: The same post asserts 'Unlike every competitor, we never fail' — an absolute comparative claim with no substantiation.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Comparative claims carry the highest substantiation burden; an AI that echoes them produces market-facing copy that is difficult to defend and easy to challenge.
the_fix: Strike the comparative claim or replace it with a specific, sourced, dated comparison.
Add comparative patterns ('unlike every competitor', 'never fail') to the banned-claims deny-list.
Route any future comparative claim through Legal sign-off.

findings.title: Outcome guarantee with a money-back promise
findings.what_we_found: The post promises 'Guaranteed to double your pipeline in 30 days or your money back' — an outcome guarantee tied to a refund.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An AI that echoes a guarantee creates direct contractual and regulatory exposure; this is the single highest-risk claim in the corpus and must be gated before any AI content step.
the_fix: Remove the guarantee and refund language immediately, pending counsel review.
Add 'guaranteed', 'double your pipeline', 'money back', and time-bound outcome promises to the banned-claims deny-list.
Require Legal/Compliance sign-off for any pricing, refund, or outcome-guarantee language, human- or AI-authored.
findings.evidence: "Guaranteed to double your pipeline in 30 days or your money back."

findings.title: No substantiation standard or review path on file
findings.what_we_found: There is no documented substantiation standard, banned-claims list, or human review/approval gate any claim must clear before publication.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Without a review path, an AI-assisted draft can reach market unchecked — the absence of a gate is itself a blocker to safely turning on any AI content step.
the_fix: Publish a substantiation standard: every superlative or comparative claim links to a dated, sourced proof artifact before use.
Maintain a banned-claims deny-list the content drafter and any AI step check against pre-publication.
Define a named human review path with Legal sign-off for guarantees, pricing, and comparative claims; log every approval.
findings.evidence: No review-gate or substantiation file referenced anywhere in the corpus.
